notes.summary: Full-boundary domain, explicit reduction and top-degree conventions, zero energy anchor, and precisely delimited qualified imports.
notes.detailedSummary: Uses only entire qualified G331 and B341 as correctness grants. Every semivaluation support remains present. Products have n-1 potential entries and energy has raw degree n. Higher-dimensional geometry and energy are reconstructed below rather than imported. Dimension zero is treated separately.
notes.text:
Let R be an excellent local ring, explicitly replaced throughout by R_red, and let n=dim R. For n>0 fix a proper maximal-ideal-primary ideal a and the compact section X_a={v:v(a)=1}. Retain all centred semivaluations, including nonminimal supports, conductor-infinite supports and lower-dimensional components.

Entire qualified G331 supplies the independently geometric class: actual negative effective finite real Cartier presentations, with nonnegative degree on every contracted integral curve, on actual primary blowups. Its continuous uniform closure C and actual decreasing-net completion D agree with the corresponding ideal classes. We use its addition, nonnegative scaling, finite maxima, upper semicontinuity, rational primary-or-unit profile density, dense ideal-difference test lattice, gauge cocycle and full normalization-fibre descent. We do not assume arbitrary-infimum or increasing-limit closure.

Entire qualified B341 supplies the bounded algebraic mixed kernel and moment measures, with n-1 potential entries, raw degree-n moments, real uniform and specified-limit bounded decreasing-net continuity, scalar ideal-moment order, one-factor gauge covariance and residue-weighted top-degree normalization. Its actual curve reference and smooth bounded BFJ comparison retain their exact scopes. It supplies no general higher-dimensional Cartier comparison, locality, energy or arbitrary finite-map theorem.

Write m_a=e_R(a)>0 and delta_a=m_a^(1/n). The additive anchor is zero. The homogeneous reference represented by -1 on X_a is -v(a); its reference measure has mass m_a, and its energy will be -m_a/n. There is no probability normalization. On a nonpure ring the chosen degree-n functional gives smaller-dimensional components zero contribution while retaining all their functions and conductor compatibility. Their own lower-dimensional energies would impose additional conditions and are not silently added.

The construction below gives a geometrically compared energy, finite-energy cone, finite positive Radon mixed measures, ordinary open locality, integrability, polynomial variations, reference cocycles and full decreasing-net continuity with specified domain limits. Its smooth convention is precisely finite BFJ Definition 4.3 local self intersection, compared directly in n8. For n=1 the operator has zero potential entries. For n=0 the boundary is empty, energy is zero and the measure is zero, without negative arity.

The unchanged original/family dossier and augmented assignment are separated in original-problem.txt, original-task.json and augmented-assignment.txt. Both complete qualified grants, including annotations, ledgers, scopes and the printed-colon qualification, are retained verbatim under inputs/grants and embedded in P12.5-paper.tex. These are unverified mathematical drafts; independent review and ROOT reading remain required.

notes.summary: Independent supported Cartier intersections: Artinian Euler polynomials, Koszul symmetry, divisor-cycle projection and raw Rees polarization.
notes.detailedSummary: Constructs intersections on actual primary models without a coefficient field, normality or Cohen–Macaulay hypothesis. Proper divisor-cycle projection preserves supported DVR degree. Eventual Rees section equality and vanishing prove exact mixed-multiplicity comparison.
notes.text:
Let Y=Bl_I R be an actual primary blowup, p=n-1 and E_I its effective exceptional Cartier divisor. Whole Stacks 31.33 gives reducedness, projectivity, the identity off the closed point, invertible image I O_Y=O_Y(-E_I), and ample O_Y(-E_I). Common product blowups dominate finite collections.

For an effective exceptional Cartier E, coherence on a finite affine cover gives m^N O_E=0. Proper cohomology is consequently of finite R-length. Define chi_R(E,F)=sum_j(-1)^j length_R H^j(E,F). For line bundles L_i, chi_R(E,O_E tensor product L_i^t_i) is a polynomial of degree at most p: filter O_E by powers of m; its finitely many coherent quotients are sheaves on a proper residue-field scheme. Tensoring is exact, and whole Stacks 33.45.1 applies to each quotient. Their supports have dimension at most p by Cartier cutting and excellent catenary dimension theory. This retains the full Artinian thickness and chooses no coefficient field.

Define Q_Y(F_1,...,F_p,E) as the coefficient of t_1...t_p for L_i=O(F_i). For p=0 it is the supported zero-dimensional length. Stacks 33.45.2 applied to the filtration gives Q=sum_Z length(O_E at eta_Z) times the numerical intersection of O(F_1),...,O(F_p) on the integral dimension-p component Z. Local composition lengths add to exactly the indicated thickened length; smaller-dimensional supports have smaller polynomial degree. Fixed twists do not change the leading coefficient.

Polynomial substitution gives symmetry and additivity in the first slots. The exact sequence 0→O_E1(-E2)→O_(E1+E2)→O_E2→0 gives last-slot additivity, since its twist changes no leading coefficient. G331's actual Cartier order unit writes any exceptional integral divisor as a difference of effective ones. Extend independently of decomposition, then by finite real multilinearity.

For full symmetry use the actual Cartier complexes K_E=[O(-E)→O] and K_F=[O(-F)→O]. Their tensor total complexes agree under signed interchange, and their cohomology is supported over an Artinian base. Their two Euler computations give chi_R(E,L)-chi_R(E,L(-F))=chi_R(F,L)-chi_R(F,L(-E)). Set L=O(F)^t O(E)^s product O(G_j)^r_j with n-2 further entries. Set t=s=0 after the differences and extract r_1...r_(n-2). The degree bound n-1 leaves only the leading monomial t product r_j on the left and s product r_j on the right. Thus the last slot exchanges with a bundle slot. Effective differences and real multilinearity prove full symmetry. No proper intersection or regularity of F on E is assumed.

For projection use delta(q)=dim R/q on Spec R. Local catenarity makes this a dimension function, also in the nonpure case; excellence supplies the universally catenary hypothesis of Stacks 42.7.1. Extend delta by residue transcendence degree on finite-type models. A proper map between primary models, or a finite normalization, maps corresponding top integral components birationally. At a generic dimension-p divisor point, the reduced one-dimensional local ring injects into its component domain quotients with finite-length cokernel. Multiplication by a regular Cartier equation has equal kernel and quotient lengths on that cokernel. Hence its Cartier cycle is the sum of the component divisor cycles. Whole Stacks 42.26.3, at function-field degree one, gives the actual cycle equality f_*[f^*E]_p=[E]_p. Smaller-dimensional components contribute no such cycle. Stacks 33.45.7 on the proper residue-field schemes then proves Q_Y'(f^*F_1,...,f^*F_n)=Q_Y(F_1,...,F_n). This preserves supported degree: on a DVR, (t) has degree one even though its global Chow class is zero. Residue degrees are retained.

For a primary I, apply whole Stacks 30.14.3 to its standard Rees algebra and the module itself: H0(Y,O_Y(-qE_I))=I^q for sufficiently large q, compatibly as actual section submodules. Whole 30.16.1(4) gives higher-cohomology vanishing. The Cartier sequence yields chi_R(E_I,O_EI(-(q-1)E_I))=length(I^(q-1)/I^q). Comparing degree-p coefficients gives -Q_Y((-E_I) repeated n)=e_R(I). On a common product blowup, the divisor of product I_j^t_j is sum t_j D_Ij. Diagonal comparison is therefore an identity of degree-n polynomials. Its t_1...t_n coefficients are -n! Q(D_I1,...,D_In) and n! e_R(I_1,...,I_n). Thus -Q equals the raw mixed multiplicity. Units give zero divisors. No coefficient inequality, generic parameter-length shortcut, CM assumption or infinite-field assumption entered this geometric comparison.

Complete proofs, exact source hypotheses and disclosed recursive dependencies are in argument.md and source-application-ledger.md. The new source applications are ordinary published applications, not additional supplied correctness grants.

notes.summary: Positive geometric core measures, refinement independence, a fixed-primary actual-image bridge, and bounded ordinary open locality.
notes.detailedSummary: Defines divisorial measures geometrically before using ideal moments. Supplies the refinement step needed for tests on larger models. One fixed Bl_(I c0) gives actual invertible section-ideal images; finite-span intersections establish comparison. Strict maximum locality extends by two compact-cover limits.
notes.text:
Normalize a primary model Y finitely to N. On each top normal component, let Z run over its exceptional dimension-p prime divisors, b_Z=ord_Z(a)>0 and v_Z=ord_Z/b_Z. For actual negative effective real curve-nef core divisors D_i define geometrically mu_Y(D_1,...,D_p)=sum_Z b_Z (O(D_1)|Z ... O(D_p)|Z . Z) delta_vZ. For p=0 the intersection is the residue-field degree of the point.

These weights are nonnegative independently of ideal moments. On the original actual primary model Y, qualified G331 gives negative rational ample L_i,j converging to D_i in finite Cartier coefficient space. Their finite-normalization pullbacks are ample by whole Stacks 29.38.7(2), since finite maps are affine and quasi-affine; restrictions to closed Z remain ample. Clear denominators and apply Stacks 33.45.9. Polynomial continuity gives nonnegative limiting weights. This uses no new Keeler application on an ungranted model.

A refinement lemma is necessary before testing on larger models. For a proper birational map between normal top components, a dimension-p exceptional prime either maps to a smaller-dimensional stratum, giving zero pulled-back p-bundle intersection by numerical projection, or dominates an exceptional prime Z. Localize at eta_Z, a DVR, and apply n2's divisor-cycle projection to a uniformizer. The sum of positive integer orders times residue degrees over Z is one. Thus precisely one prime dominates Z, its order and residue degree are one, and its DVR valuation equals that of Z: both DVRs have the same fraction field and the second dominates the first, so writing field elements as uniformizer powers times units forces equal orders. Projection preserves the intersection weight and b_Z. Normalizations of common primary refinements map to N componentwise. Therefore these atomic measures are unchanged on the boundary under primary refinement.

For a Cartier test F on the model, H_F(v_Z)=ord_Z(F)/b_Z. The normal divisor cycle and n2 give integral H_F dmu_Y=Q_Y(D_1,...,D_p,F). The refinement lemma extends this to tests determined on a larger common primary model.

To compare real cores with the algebraic kernel, fix one Y=Bl_I R. Qualified G331 gives T=H0(Y,O_Y), an h with m^h(T/R)=0, and the fixed primary c0=m^(h+1) satisfying c0 T⊂m as elements of R. For a negative rational ample L and sufficiently large divisible q, O_Y(qL) is generated. Put J_q=c0 H0(Y,O_Y(qL)). It is an actual proper ideal of R and is unit off the closed point by localization of sections, hence primary. Fix exactly one refinement Y'=Bl_(I c0) R and let D0 be the pulled-back negative divisor of c0. Pulling back the generating surjection and multiplying by the invertible c0 image gives the actual image identity J_q O_Y'=O_Y'(q f^*L+D0). The Cartier inclusion remains injective because its equation is nonzero on every reduced generic component. This is not merely equality of valuations. The blowup universal property gives Y'→Bl_Jq R.

N2 now gives e(J_1,q1,...,J_n,qn)/product q_i=-Q_Y'(f^*L_1+D0/q1,...,f^*L_n+D0/qn). All intersections lie on this one model. Evaluations satisfy -v(J_q)/q=H_L-v(c0)/q, uniformly since c0 is primary. Approximate each real nef D_i by G331's negative rational ample L_i,j on Y, using the same c0 and Y' for every i,j, and choose generated divisible q_i,j→infinity. Polynomial intersection continuity and B341's uniform moment continuity give the identical limit. Hence the bounded algebraic full form on cores is -Q. Every Cartier test F is a difference of negative ample exceptional divisors, by a sufficiently large ample/order-unit shift F-N E_I and -N E_I. Extend the comparison by linearity and common refinements. Dense ideal-difference tests and finite mass identify mu_Y with B341's measure on every core tuple, proving actual presentation and primary-model independence.

For strict maximum locality synchronize denominators: u=-v(A)/q, w=-v(B)/q and max(u,w)=-v(A+B)/q. On a common normalized primary model make these ideals and all other inputs invertible. Divide A and B by S=(A+B)O_N to obtain actual invertible subideals L,M⊂O_N with L+M=O_N. At a prime Z with u(v_Z)>w(v_Z), ord_Z(M)>0. The restricted map M|Z→O_Z vanishes generically and hence everywhere because Z is integral. Thus L|Z→O_Z is an isomorphism. D_A|Z and D_(A+B)|Z consequently have identical bundle classes and mixed weights. On their common atomic support, mu(max(u,w),others)|{u>w}=mu(u,others)|{u>w}. Unit cases are included.

Uniform rational approximation extends this to continuous u,w and other continuous inputs: a test with compact support inside {u>w} has a uniform positive gap there. Bounded decreasing representations extend the other slots to bounded D, with the open region fixed.

Uniform weak continuity inside bounded D follows separately from scalar moment order. If tuples lie in [-M,0] and differ uniformly by at most epsilon, compare u_i-epsilon≤w_i and conversely, then expand the negative constant shifts. For each primary J the moment difference is at most ((M+epsilon)^p-M^p)e(a repeated p,J). Dense tests and common masses give weak continuity. No increasing-limit membership is asserted.

Finally let bounded u,w∈D agree on open U. Choose bounded actual decreasing C representations u_alpha,w_beta. For a test supported on compact K⊂U, fixed alpha and epsilon>0, the directed open sets {w_beta-epsilon<u_alpha} cover K. One beta_0 gives an open neighbourhood of K valid for every later beta. Strict continuous locality identifies the integrals for max(u_alpha,w_beta-epsilon) and u_alpha. First take the specified bounded beta limit to max(u_alpha,w-epsilon), then the alpha limit to max(u,w-epsilon). Reverse u,w. Both maximum functions are uniformly within epsilon of the already known D function max(u,w), so uniform weak continuity gives the same limit. Radon regularity and Urysohn tests identify restrictions on U. Replace slots successively for full bounded mixed ordinary open locality. These are two justified limits, not an assumed flattening theorem.

notes.summary: Full bounded symmetric n-form and discontinuous test pairing; arbitrary fixed-slot Cauchy, generalized Holder, Minkowski and concavity.
notes.detailedSummary: Proves directed integration for continuous families rather than testing weak measures with discontinuous functions. Three multiplicities use the same superficial two-dimensional quotient, retaining non-CM, embedded and lower-dimensional issues. A finite integer-simplex maximum argument proves the full n-entry inequality.
notes.text:
For rational primary-or-unit profiles u_i=-v(I_i)/q_i define F(u_1,...,u_n)=e_R(I_1,...,I_n)/product q_i. B341's kernel makes this presentation independent, symmetric, additive, nonnegative and order-reversing relative to functions in every slot. If entries lie in [-M,0], F≤M^n m_a. Negative-constant shifts bound the difference of uniformly epsilon-close tuples by ((M+epsilon)^n-M^n)m_a. Uniform rational approximation therefore defines the same real form on C.

For bounded D entries choose actual decreasing C representations in every slot. Their forms increase and remain bounded. Representation independence follows from directed compact open covers: for a fixed C majorant h_i≥u_i, the sets {g_i,alpha<h_i+epsilon} cover X. Select one eventual index in every slot; then g_i,alpha-epsilon≤h_i. Order and the shift error compare F(h) to the representation supremum. Reverse representations and let epsilon vanish. This proves F(u)=sup{F(h):h_i∈C,h_i≥u_i}, as well as order on bounded D. Actual product-index representations prove addition and scaling. The same USC open-cover argument proves bounded decreasing-net continuity when the specified D limit and a common bound are given.

For a continuous C test v, ideal approximation and B341's weak continuity give F(v,u_1,...,u_p)=integral(-v)dmu(u_1,...,u_p). To extend to an actual discontinuous bounded D test, the required directed Radon lemma is: if f_alpha are directed increasing nonnegative continuous functions on compact Hausdorff X and f=sup f_alpha, then integral f dσ=sup integral f_alpha dσ for every finite positive Radon σ. For a continuous nonnegative h≤f, directed compactness of {f_alpha>h-epsilon} gives one index and an integral lower bound integral h-epsilon σ(X). Moreover integral f is the supremum of such continuous-minorant integrals: truncate f, partition its range, approximate each open superlevel set from inside by a compact set, and use Urysohn functions supported in the corresponding superlevel sets. The sum of step increments times these functions is ≤f, and its integral approaches the step integral. Let compact errors and step size vanish, then let the truncation level grow. This proves the lemma even for infinite f. Arbitrary measurable-net monotone convergence would be false.

Apply the lemma to -g_alpha increasing to -v for an actual C representation of the bounded D test, against the fixed mixed measure. For each g_alpha the continuous-test identity holds. Commuting its supremum with the independent potential-representation suprema proves the full bounded identity F(v,others)=integral(-v)dmu(others).

For the new inequality, complete SH17.7.1 applies to any two-dimensional Noetherian local ring and finite dimension-two module. Its proof chooses a two-generated reduction (a,b) of I after exact R(z). For positive r,s,N, length(M/I^(rN)J^(sN)M)≤2 length(M/J^(sN)M)+length(M/(a^(rN),b^(rN))M). Divide by N^2/2 and use Lech's parameter asymptotics, power and reduction invariance. This gives e(I^rJ^s)≤2e(I)r^2+2e(J)s^2. Expand the left side; optimize positive rational r/s to obtain e(I,J)^2≤e(I)e(J), using mixed positivity. Complete immediate SH17.7.1–3 and the used superficial units were read; earlier reduction/Lech foundations are honestly disclosed in the ledger.

For arbitrary fixed proper K_3,...,K_n, choose one element in K_3 simultaneously superficial for the three families (K,I,I), (K,I,J), (K,J,J), and avoiding minimal primes. SH17.2.2 removes finitely many proper subspaces of the same K_3/mK_3; their common complement has a point over an infinite field. SH17.4.6 reduces all three multiplicities on the same quotient of dimension n-1. Repeat in the remaining fixed slots to obtain the same two-dimensional quotient for all three. Quotients may be nonreduced, non-CM and have embedded or smaller-dimensional components; no regular sequence or deletion is assumed. Finite residue fields use R(z), preserving dimension and every finite-length polynomial by composition series, without identifying boundaries. Therefore F(x,y,K)^2≤F(x,x,K)F(y,y,K). Unit entries follow by adding -epsilon v(a); real C and bounded D cases follow by proved form limits. The literal unquotiented infinite-length colon in SH17.4.7 is never used: its correction is the finite annihilator on the quotient by previous parameters.

For full n-entry Holder, consider a finite integer simplex of counts alpha_i≥0, sum alpha_i=n, of proper ideal types. Set f(alpha)=log F(types^alpha)-sum alpha_i log F(type_i repeated n)/n. All values are finite by primary positivity and vertices have value zero. Conditional Cauchy gives 2f(alpha)≤f(alpha+e_i-e_j)+f(alpha-e_i+e_j) whenever both selected counts are positive. If the finite maximum were positive, choose a maximizer of smallest support. Both neighbours must also maximize. Repeated transfer from j to i reaches a maximizer with smaller support, a contradiction. Hence F(u_1,...,u_n)≤product A(u_i), where A(u)=F(u repeated n)^(1/n). Perturbation and the established form limits include zero/unit/real/bounded-D cases.

Expand F((u+w) repeated n) and apply Holder termwise to get Minkowski A(u+w)≤A(u)+A(w). For a signed cone difference z=U-V, conditional Cauchy implies F(z,z,K)=F(U,U,K)+F(V,V,K)-2F(U,V,K)≥0. Thus E_bd=-F(u repeated n)/n is concave along every bounded admissible segment: its second derivative is -(n-1)F(z,z,u_t repeated n-2). For n=1 it is linear. No norm separation, strictness or uniqueness is inferred in nonpure rings.

notes.summary: Truncation finite energy, full majorant formula, noncircular approximation without a common bound, cone closure and full decreasing-net measures.
notes.detailedSummary: Finite target sizes control shift errors before unbounded additivity is established. Cone closure is proved first. Ideal moments and uniform masses construct canonical Radon measures. Net continuity requires a specified D/E1 limit; arbitrary-infimum and increasing closure are not claimed.
notes.text:
For u∈D put u^k=max(u,-k), a bounded D function. Define F_infinity(u_1,...,u_n)=sup_(k_i) F(u_1^k1,...,u_n^kn), E(u)=-F_infinity(u repeated n)/n, and E1={u∈D:E(u)>-infinity}. Integer cutoffs are cofinal with real cutoffs.

For every D tuple, including infinite-energy tuples, F_infinity(u)=sup{F(h):h_i∈C,h_i≥u_i}. Indeed a fixed finite continuous majorant h dominates u^k once k≥its bound, so its form is ≤the cutoff supremum. Conversely the bounded majorant formula for each truncation uses only continuous majorants that also dominate u. This proves both inequalities without a lower bound on u or a new completion closure.

Let A_i=F_infinity(u_i repeated n)^(1/n). Holder on truncations gives F_infinity(u_1,...,u_n)≤product A_i for E1 entries. Every D majorant of an E1 function is E1 with no larger size. Global bottom has infinite energy because F((-k) repeated n)=k^n m_a. Lower-dimensional poles invisible to top degree remain legitimate domain points.

Before unbounded additivity, prove the following approximation lemma. Let individually bounded D functions f_i,lambda decrease to specified E1 targets u_i, without a common finite lower bound. For a fixed C majorant tuple h_i≥u_i, the USC open sets {f_i,lambda<h_i+epsilon} cover X. Directed compactness gives a common eventual index with f_i,lambda-epsilon≤h_i. Each term has diagonal size at most A_i. Bounded additivity and Holder give a uniform scalar shift bound: 0≤F(f_1,lambda-epsilon,...,f_n,lambda-epsilon)-F(f_lambda)≤product(A_i+epsilon delta_a)-product A_i. Order compares the shifted tuple to h. Let epsilon vanish and take the full majorant supremum. Hence F(f_lambda) increases to F_infinity(u). Separate indices use their actual finite product directed set. This proof uses bounded additivity only.

Now prove E1 cone closure. For u,w∈E1, s_k=u^k+w^k decreases to u+w∈D by the granted actual product-representation addition rule. Bounded Minkowski gives A(s_k)≤A(u)+A(w). For each C majorant h≥u+w, a compact strict-test cover selects k with s_k-epsilon≤h. Thus F(h repeated n)≤(A(u)+A(w)+epsilon delta_a)^n. The majorant formula proves u+w∈E1 and Minkowski there. Positive scaling uses cofinal rescaled cutoffs; scalar zero is separate. Only after this closure proof apply the approximation lemma to sums of truncations and the other truncated entries. Bounded additivity passes to finite limits. Thus F_infinity is a finite symmetric additive cone n-form on E1, with real homogeneity, order, conditional Cauchy, Holder, Minkowski and concavity.

For E1 entries u_1,...,u_p, their truncation measures have primary moments F(u_1^k1,...,u_p^kp,-v(J)), increasing to the finite value F_infinity(u_1,...,u_p,-v(J)). Their masses are bounded by delta_a product A_i. Difference-lattice integrals consequently converge, preserving positivity, with a common norm bound. Density extends the limit to a unique positive continuous functional on C(X), hence a finite positive Radon measure mu_E. Uniform approximation of a continuous test by a lattice test, with the common mass bound, proves actual weak net convergence without metrizability or subsequences. Its moment identity is integral v(J)dmu_E=F_infinity(u_1,...,u_p,-v(J)). The approximation lemma gives the same convergence for every individually bounded decreasing D approximation of these targets, making the construction canonical and agreeing with B341 on bounded inputs. Additivity follows from moments and density.

For an arbitrary decreasing E1 net u_i,lambda with specified E1 limit u_i in D, sizes are bounded by the target sizes. Compare to each C majorant using the same USC compact covers. The already established unbounded multilinearity and Holder give the same uniform shift error. Taking epsilon to zero and the majorant supremum proves F_infinity(u_lambda) increases to F_infinity(u). Fixing the last primary test gives all moment limits and the common mass bound gives weak mixed-measure convergence. Diagonals give E(u_lambda) decreasing to E(u). These are full directed-net statements.

If a decreasing E1 net has a specified D limit and uniformly bounded sizes, the same majorant argument first proves that limit is E1, then gives the preceding continuity. It never asserts D membership of an arbitrary infimum.

notes.summary: Extended test pairing, E1 integrability, polynomial variation, reference cocycles, elementary capacity and finite-energy open locality.
notes.detailedSummary: Actual C representations and commuting justified scalar suprema prove unbounded pairing. Every E1 test is integrable against every finite-energy mixed measure. The capacity estimate proves pole capacity zero without Choquet, quasicontinuity, Borel cutoff or uniqueness claims.
notes.text:
For v∈E1 choose an actual decreasing C representation g_alpha→v. Each term is bounded and has size at most A(v). Apply n4's directed Radon lemma to -g_alpha increasing to -v against the fixed finite-energy measure. For fixed g_alpha, continuous-test weak convergence identifies its integral with sup_(k_i) F(g_alpha,u_1^k1,...,u_p^kp). These nonnegative scalar suprema commute. N5's approximation lemma applies to the product net of individually bounded functions with finite-energy targets. Therefore integral(-v)dmu_E(u_1,...,u_p)=F_infinity(v,u_1,...,u_p)≤A(v) product A(u_i)<infinity. This is actual integrability, not weak convergence tested with an unbounded function. Every such measure assigns zero mass to every E1 test's pole set. In particular E(u)=(1/n) integral u dmu_E(u repeated p).

For any v∈D, possibly outside E1, apply the preceding identity to bounded v^k. Ordinary nonnegative sequence integration and cofinal commuting cutoff suprema give integral(-v)dmu_E(others)=F_infinity(v,others) in [0,infinity]. Finiteness is asserted when v∈E1 or that mixed value is finite.

Finite polynomial multilinearity gives d/dt E(u+tv)=-F_infinity(v,(u+tv) repeated p)=integral v dmu_E((u+tv) repeated p), for t≥0, one-sided at zero. Signed admissible directions are differences of E1 cone entries; their absolute integrability follows by applying the pairing separately. Conditional Cauchy makes the second derivative nonpositive, proving concavity on finite-energy segments.

For a finite-energy reference w define E_w(u)=E(u)-E(w). Telescoping the symmetric n-form gives E_w(u)=(1/n) sum_(j=0)^p integral(u-w)dmu_E(u repeated j,w repeated p-j). Every term is absolutely integrable. Consequently E_w(u)+E_z(w)=E_z(u). This includes anchor zero, E(0)=0, E(-1)=-m_a/n and reference mass m_a. A globally zero potential entry annihilates positive-arity products; the zero-arity curve operator remains its fixed reference measure.

For Borel A define Cap_a(A)=sup{mu(phi repeated p)(A):phi∈bounded D,-1≤phi≤0}. It is monotone, countably subadditive and at most m_a: each measure has these properties and sup of a sum is bounded by the sum of suprema. Since A(phi)≤delta_a, the pairing gives Cap_a({u<-t})≤A(u) delta_a^p/t. Every E1 pole set thus has capacity zero. This proves neither Choquet regularity nor quasicontinuity, and no measure order follows from scalar moment order.

If E1 tuples agree on an open U, their constant truncations agree there. N3 gives equality of bounded restrictions. Tests supported on compact subsets of U pass to the finite-energy weak limits; Urysohn functions and Radon regularity identify the restrictions. This proves ordinary open locality. A strict Borel set {u>-k} need not be open for USC u, so no nonpluripolar Borel cutoff identity is asserted or used. Equation uniqueness is also not inferred.

notes.summary: Primary energy invariance with one measure factor; weighted normalization, full conductor E1 descent, actual curves and empty case.
notes.detailedSummary: Variable primary cutoffs are squeezed between cofinal constant cutoffs. Normalization retains total residue degrees, including inseparability, and all conductor supports. Only top-dimensional centres contribute to the chosen degree-n energy; lower-dimensional compatibility is retained.
notes.text:
For another primary b put d(v)=v_a(b), T(v)=v/d(v), with 0<d_min≤d≤d_max on X_a, and u_b(Tv)=u_a(v)/d(v). G331 transports actual C and D representations. B341's bounded law is mu_b=T_*[d mu_a]. Pair an additional bounded D test using n4; its division by d cancels that single factor, proving invariance of the full bounded n-form.

The b-truncation of an unbounded u pulls back homogeneously to w_k=max(u_a,-kd), a bounded D function since -kd is a primary profile. It satisfies max(u_a,-k d_max)≤w_k≤max(u_a,-k d_min). The constant cutoff levels are cofinal. Bounded invariance and scalar order therefore prove diagonal F_infinity and energy invariance, including infinite values, and equivalence of E1 membership. For E1 tuples, w_i,k are individually bounded decreasing approximants; n5 extends the full form identity and the measure law by weak limits tested with the fixed continuous multiplier d. Thus E_b(u_b)=E_a(u_a) and mu_E,b=T_*[d mu_E,a]. There is exactly one measure factor. For b=a^r it is r, while potentials divide by r. notes.text:
The primary smooth source is published BFJ, Valuations and plurisubharmonic singularities, particularly the complete Setting, Proposition 1.14, relevant 2.4–2.8 units and entire Section 4 including Definition 4.3. Its hypotheses are exactly a smooth closed point of an affine variety over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, n≥2, initially with maximal-ideal section. G331 supplies the whole formal-psh class comparison on all semivaluations with bottom adjoined; B341 supplies bounded operator comparison. Neither is an unbounded energy citation.

Specify the canonical smooth local convention explicitly. For a BFJ formal psh g with nef Weil divisor Z(g), define E_BFJ,int(g)=<Z(g) repeated n>/n and E1_BFJ,int by finite self intersection. The bracket is precisely Definition 4.3: the infimum of intersections of nef Cartier majorants. This selects a published local primary intersection extension, zero anchor and raw degree n, rather than a degree n+1 projective energy or a probability normalization. We do not claim BFJ uses this E1 notation or states a separately named unbounded energy theorem.

For a nef Cartier W, its function w is continuous and belongs to C by BFJ 1.14 and G331. Coefficientwise W≥Z(u) is equivalent to w≥u on the entire section. Coefficient order gives order at divisorial points; on each closed simplex both formal functions are continuous and rational divisorial points are dense, so it gives order at every quasi-monomial. Their canonical all-retraction infima preserve that order on every semivaluation. The reverse implication follows already on divisorial points. B341's bounded operator and n4's bounded test identity give F(w_1,...,w_n)=-<W_1,...,W_n>.

Thus minus Definition 4.3's intersection is the supremum over these Cartier majorants, at most the full C-majorant supremum defining F_infinity. For the reverse bound fix C majorants h_i≥u_i. If any h_i=0 its form value is zero. Otherwise the granted normal zero dichotomy gives h_i≤-c_i<0 uniformly. Approximate (1-eta)h_i by a rational primary profile r_i,eta with uniform error less than eta c_i/2. Then r_i,eta≥h_i+eta c_i/2≥u_i, so each is a nef Cartier majorant, and r_i,eta→h_i uniformly. Uniform form continuity proves F(h) is at most the Cartier-majorant supremum. Therefore F_infinity(u_1,...,u_n)=-<Z(u_1),...,Z(u_n)> in [0,infinity]. Zero entries agree separately. Global bottom has infinite self energy and is excluded from E1; every other D function is the full BFJ function by G331.

This proves equality of the entire finite-energy spaces and energies under the stated canonical convention, not merely bounded/core agreement. Holder makes the mixed mass with Z(m) finite for E1 tuples. BFJ 4.6's characterization at that finite mass, the ideal moment identity and the comparison just proved identify mu_E with its local intersection operator. Integrability of E1 tests is independently established in n6. N5 proves uniqueness of its bounded decreasing extension for every individually bounded approximation of a specified E1 target. General primary gauges use n7's proved transport; no unpublished arbitrary-gauge BFJ theorem is attributed to the source. DVR and empty cases are direct.

No singular or positive-characteristic multiplier/resolution scope is broadened. No forced equality with Cegrell spaces of classical psh germs or global projective BJ energy is asserted. Qualified G331's nodal mixed-zero literal classical/CLD radial obstruction remains unchanged.
